text:
maria: FYI saw a weird p99 swing on /v1/generate after this morning's quota/routing change. Console shows ~900ms but logs don't.
jake: Same. Rollout note mentioned 'prefer-low-latency' but didn't mention sample attribution - did routing weights change?
deploy-bot: policy:update at 1767771000 by @ops -> prefer-low-latency weight 0.6
sophia: Do we compute percentiles by merging per-route tdigest digests or recomputing from raw rows? If we merge digests, a small high-latency route can skew merged p99 when its weight increases.
maria: Console uses ingestion tdigest rollups, merged at query time. That can diverge from raw-row percentiles, especially with sparse shards or different sketch resolutions.
jake: Local repro: per-route p99s = [routeA: 440ms, routeB: 1850ms], raw combined p99 = 510ms, console merged p99 ~900ms. So merged digest != raw aggregation.
alex: We should surface per-route percentiles in the latency pane and add provenance info explaining aggregation method and sample counts.
sophia: Also propose a debug button to run an exact raw-row percentile SQL for audits and a dashboard warning when merged vs raw differs >15%.
maria: Action items: @jake add per-route p50/p95/p99 UI + tooltip, @alex add backend endpoint exposing per-route raw counts and audit SQL, @sophia draft alert rule and support blurb, I'll notify CS after deploy.
jake: Opening PR now with screenshots and tests comparing sketch-merge vs raw on synthetic data.
alex: I'll add a backend flag and gate the UI behind a feature flag.
sophia: UX note: avoid 'tdigest' wording for customers; use 'sampled merge' and 'may differ from exact raw percentile'.
maria: Thanks — we'll ship behind flag and follow up with short post-deploy note for CSM.
